notes: Paper is Michalak et al. 2016, wheat (cv. Akteur), Poland, 2014/2015 season. Five seaweed/algae extract treatments compared against untreated control: (1) Baltic macroalgae 1.0 L/ha, (2) Ascophyllum nodosum 1.0 L/ha, (3) Spirulina platensis 1.0 L/ha, (4) Spirulina platensis 1.5 L/ha, (5) Spirulina platensis 1.8 L/ha. GT ctrl_mean=0.945 is exactly 10x smaller than JSON ctrl_mean=9.45 — unit difference (GT likely in some scaled unit, JSON in t/ha). Four of five GT-to-JSON matches are near-perfect on effect size. The fifth (GT513 vs json_idx 16, Spirulina 1.0) shows opposite sign (+1.06% GT vs -0.53% JSON), suggesting a possible extraction error in the Spirulina 1.0 treatment vs control assignment in the JSON. The AI extractor also captured many non-yield observations (ear morphology, grain components) which are correctly excluded from the Li 2022 yield meta-analysis.
